title: M2: Sandbox — block network and credentials for student code
description: Intent: As the maintainer, I want student programs to run without network access or cloud credentials, so that untrusted code cannot reach the internet or the AWS account. Includes: small C launcher using libseccomp (denies socket for AF_INET/AF_INET6, no_new_privs), scrubbed environment, no task-role permissions, ulimits/process caps against fork bombs, proof on real Fargate. Excludes: private-subnet/VPC-endpoint egress blocking (revisit if more students join). DoD: Python socket.connect and C connect() fail with EPERM; credential/metadata reads fail; specs pass locally and on Fargate.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Runner sandbox/interactive code reviewed independently. Review reproduced three high-severity exploits (student reads server secrets via /proc, kills the runner, escapes process-group kill and wedges a slot). Fixes in progress: per-run unprivileged uid, kill-by-uid cleanup, /tmp cleanup and disk watchdog, extended seccomp denylist.

comments.author: home
comments.text: M2 done: specs pass, two adversarial reviews, per-run uid, seccomp, cleanup. Fargate confirmation tracked separately.

right_now_summary: The sandbox passes core tests, while fixes address secret leaks, runner kills, and process cleanup.
